note: The English teen edition quotes the ESV in each chapter's epigraph. ESV wording cannot be carried into Portuguese, and the language's Bible (porbrbsl, Bíblia Livre — Almeida tradition) was unreachable from the worker session (api.takeroot.bible egress-blocked), so every epigraph was rendered in the Almeida register the shipped pt corpus quotes and the “(ESV)” label was dropped. Where a shipped *.pt.json carries the words verbatim they were pasted and the row is `mined` with that file; otherwise the row is `self_rendered` in the Almeida register and needs a check against porbrbsl.

Mined epigraphs: Luke 18:1, Philippians 4:19, Psalm 118:17 and Matthew 18:19 (whole verse). Mined fragments in the body: Matthew 5:42a, John 3:16a, Isaiah 53:3a, Matthew 5:39a, Romans 13:8a, Matthew 6:11. Matthew 9:37–38 keeps women-who-moved-heaven-2.pt's words of Jesus but adds the ESV's narrative frame (“Então disse aos seus discípulos”), so it ships `self_rendered`; John 19:30, Proverbs 19:17, Psalm 107:29, 1 Corinthians 9:22, Matthew 8:20, Romans 12:21 and Psalm 34:10 are self-rendered outright (the corpus has none of them whole).

Chapter 11's scroll mottos (“Até aqui o Senhor nos ajudou”, “O Senhor proverá”) match a-retrospect-children.pt, whose own notes record them as self_rendered — so they are self_rendered here too. Luke 18:1b (“e nunca desfaleçam”) is the body's second-person echo of the mined epigraph, so it is ours.

Title is “Retrospecto (Para Jovens)”, not “(Para Adolescentes)”: Hudson Taylor's covers use the rail layout, which caps a painted-cover title at 28 characters (coverLayouts.test.ts), and “Retrospecto (Para Adolescentes)” is 31. “Retrospecto” follows a-retrospect-children.pt (renamed for the same limit). Money is kept British (meia-coroa, xelins, pence, soberano, libras — the a-retrospect-guide.pt wording for “um xelim e seis pence”); the Chinese “cash” coin is “caixa”, its historical Portuguese name; miles are converted to km.
